confidence_notes: I ran five web searches: one for the RBA rate and four for Siargao prices. They returned mostly undated or older blogs, travel-cost aggregators and resort guides, which disagree with each other. Meal anchors rest on the best-supported figures: local meals at roughly PHP 150-250 and mid-range pizza or pasta at PHP 250-400, with a mid-range meal at about $9 and a mid-range dinner for two at about $20 in aggregators. I set the two-person mid-range meal above that aggregator figure because General Luna tourist-area prices are the highest on the island. Coffee is based on a cup at about PHP 90-130 and a cappuccino at about $2 in the sources, nudged up for a tourist cafe. Beer is based on San Miguel at about $1.50-2 in the sources, and I assumed restaurant pricing. The searches found no direct Siargao price for cocktails or wine. The cocktail anchor uses an aggregator's roughly $5 average, which is about 2.5 times beer. The wine anchor is a judgement that imported wine by the glass costs somewhat more than a cocktail. Wine is the weakest estimate. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of Siargao, where General Luna and Cloud 9 are high-demand surf-tourism areas. They are not based on live listings. Sources also conflict on the PHP/USD rate (about 56 to 64), which adds uncertainty. Estimates are for General Luna and may be lower elsewhere on the island. Prices may also differ from July 2026 peak-season levels.
comparable_city_reasoning: Siargao (General Luna) is treated as a Philippine island surf-tourism hub. It is cheaper than Boracay and El Nido at the top end, with local eateries very cheap and tourist-oriented cafes, bars and boutique stays priced well above local norms. It is somewhat comparable to Canggu or Ubud in Bali, but a little cheaper.
